title: Combining electrophysiology and optogenetics for functional screening of pyramidal neurons in the mouse prefrontal cortex
protocol: Construct plasmids expressing RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated single gene knockdown and scramble vectors.
Use BLOCK-iT Pol II miR RNAi Expression Vector Kit for construction of the miRNA plasmids.
Exclude possible side effects of GFP expression by using an empty vector carrying only GFP without miRNA sequences as control miRNA vector.
Mix 5 μL each of the top- and bottom-oligonucleotides constructed in the step “Design and Generation of Oligonucleotides for RNA Interference (RNAi)-Mediated Knockdown Experiment”.
Add 1 μL of oligo annealing buffer to the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 84°C for 4 min.
Mix 1 μL of the 500×-eluted oligonucleotides and 0.5 μL pCAG-GFP empty vector without any inserted miRNA oligonucleotides with 1.5 μL Ligation high Ver. 2 at 24°C–27°C for 1h.
Transform all of these samples into 50 μL of competent cells.
Incubate the sample on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the sample at 42°C for 30 s.
Incubate the sample on ice for 2 min.
Add warm 250 μL S.O.C. medium to the sample.
Incubate it at 37°C for 45–60 min.
Spread the sample evenly on an LB agar plate with ampicillin.
Pick several colonies from the LB plate using plastic tips.
Put each tip into a tube of 3 mL 2% LB medium with 300 μg ampicillin sodium.
Incubate the tubes for 12–16 h at 37°C.
Use 1 mL of the 3 mL LB medium with the competent cells to make a glycerol stock for long-term storage at -80°C.
Use what is leftover of the 3 mL LB medium and competent cell mixture for mini-prep.
Design forward and reverse PCR primers for the cDNA to clone whole sequences of the targeted gene.
Order the designed primers commercially.

Vortex a pre-mixed master solution containing 4 μL 10× PCR buffer, 4 μL dNTPs, 2.4 μL MgSO4, 2.4 μL primer mix (1.2 μL forward and 1.2 μL reverse primers) (10 μM), 1.6 μL cDNA library, and 24.8 μL MilliQ water for each reaction.
Add 0.8 μL of DNA polymerase per reaction to the pre-mixed master solution.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Add 40 μL of the pre-mixed master solution into each 200 μL PCR tube.
Run the PCR using an appropriate program.
Perform 1.5% agarose gel electrophoresis using the PCR samples.
Extract the band from the agarose gel under UV light.
Purify the PCR product from the extracted band using the DNA purification kit.
Mix 1 μL of the PCR product with 1 μL of linearized pCAG-mOrange empty vector and 2 μL of Ligation high Ver. 2.
Incubate this mixture at 24°C–27°C for 1 h.
Transform and isolate the plasmid as shown in the construction of the KD-miRNA plasmid.
Check the insertion of the cDNA sequence using restriction enzymes and agarose gel electrophoresis.
Design primers using the QuikChange Primer Design site.
Replace 4–6 nucleotides in the miRNA-targeted sequences without changing any codons from the DNA sequences.

Mix 1 μL forward and 1 μL reverse primers (125 ng/μL each) with 1 μl WT-cDNA plasmid (50 ng/μL), 5 μl 10× reaction buffer, 1 μl dNTP mix, 1.5 μl QuikSolution reagent and 38.5 μl MilliQ water in 200 μl PCR tubes.
Vortex the mixture well.
Add 1 μl QuikChange Lightning Enzyme into each PCR tube.
Mix it gently by pipetting.
Run the PCR using appropriate program.
Apply 2 μl Dpn I restriction enzyme to the PCR mixed sample.
Mix it gently by pipetting.
Incubate it at 37°C for 5 min.
Transform the sample into the competent cells as explained from Protocol No. 5 to No. 19 in step 1-1.
Validate miRNAs on HEK293T cells before applying them to in vivo experiments.
Quantify mRNA expression by qPCR using the electroporated brain to confirm the reduction of the targeted gene.
Prepare a 100 mm dish with 50% confluent HEK293T cells.
Replace the medium with HBSS (3 mL).
Add trypsin (500 μL) to the dish containing HBSS.
Incubate the dish for 3–5 min at 37°C in a 95% O2 and 5% CO2 environment.
Add 7 mL of HBSS to the dish and mix well.
Centrifuge the mixture in a 50 mL tube at 110 × g for 3 min at any temperature below 20°C.
Remove the supernatant and suspend the cells in 12 mL of DMEM medium.
Put 0.5 mL of suspended cell solution into each well of a 24-well plate for cell culture (Nunc Multidish 24 NunclonTM Delta Surface).
Prepare four 1.5 mL-tubes containing OPTI-MEM (50 μL/well; 300 μL/6 wells).
Add mixed plasmids to the four 1.5-mL tubes for different conditions.
Add 1.5 μL of X-tremeGeneTM HP DNA Transfection Reagent to each tube and keep at 24°C–27°C for 15 min.
Add the transfection mixture to each well containing HEK 293T cells.
Repeat steps from preparation to addition of transfection mixture after 6 hours.
Remove the medium and add 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) into each well.
Keep the plate at 24°C–27°C for 10 min.
Remove the PFA and wash three times using phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add 300 μL PBS containing 0.1% Triton X to each well.
Keep at 24°C–27°C for 10 min.
Add 30 μL of donkey serum (as a blocking agent) to each well.
Keep at 24°C–27°C for 30 min.
Wash the wells with PBS three times.
Add primary antibody for GFP (diluted 1:1000 with PBS) and RFP (diluted 1:300 with PBS).
Keep the samples at 4°C for 12–24 h.
Wash the wells with PBS three times.
Incubate in the secondary antibody (diluted 1:400 with PBS) at 24°C–27°C for 1 hour.
Perform confocal imaging of the fluorescent signals from each well.
Capture 5-6 images per well to quantify the fluorescent signals.
Transfect several types of combinations composed of different plasmids using in utero electroporation.
Mix the solution containing the plasmid and inject it into one side of the lateral ventricles on each embryo.
Position the injection site at 0.75–1.0 mm anterior from lambda and 0.5 mm lateral from the sagittal suture.
Place the negative pole of the bipolar electrode over the injected hemisphere and the positive pole on the contralateral side.
Angle the two electrodes rostrocaudally and vertically for optimal targeting of the mPFC.
Deliver electrical stimulation via the forceps-shaped bipolar electrode to perform electroporation.
Prepare injection glass pipettes using a micropipette puller with settings: Step1 HEAT=602, PULL=35, VEL=200, Time=250; Step2 HEAT 604, PULL=0, VEL=200, TIME=250.
Anesthetize a pregnant ICR mouse at embryonic day 14.5.
Open the abdominal wall and create a 3–5 cm hole using surgical scissors.
Gently pick up each pup from the hole on the abdomen with round-shaped forceps.
Inject a 2–3 μL solution, including a single plasmid or combination of several plasmids, into a lateral ventricle.
Keep the embryo wet using autoclaved PBS during the operation.
Set the bipolar electrode to target the mPFC.
Deliver electrical stimulations (35 V for 50 ms) five times at 950 ms intervals via forceps-shaped bipolar electrodes connected to the electroporator.
Suture the abdominal hole using surgical strings.
Inject painkillers into the abdomen.
Express an opsin sparsely in a subset of KD neurons using the Cre-loxP system.
Transfect 1–2 μg/μl of pCAG-DIO-Chronos-GFP plasmid and 1–2 μg/μl of pCAG-KD-miRNA-mOrange plasmid into L2/3 pyramidal neurons.
Co-transfect a smaller dose (0.5–1 ng/μl) of pCAG-Cre plasmid with the opsin and KD-miRNA plasmids for sparse labeling.
Use an extremely light-sensitive opsin such as Chronos for the experiment.
Verify fluorescent expression in each pup through the skull with green/red-light glasses 1–3 days after birth.
Select pups carrying efficient fluorescent expression.
Prepare recording patch pipettes from borosilicate glass capillary using the Micropipette Puller.
Chill the cutting solution on ice for 30 min–1 h bubbled with mixed gas composed of 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Anesthetize and sacrifice a mouse in accordance with your approved Institutional Animal Care Use Committee (IACUC) protocol.
Remove the brain from the mouse immediately (< 1 min).
Put the brain into the cold cutting solution on ice.
Incubate the brain in the cutting solution for around 3 min.
Trim the posterior part of the brain at +1.0 to +2.0 mm anteriorly from the bregma.
Set the trimmed brain at the chamber of the slicer.
Start to cut the brain slices in the cold cutting solution.
Cut 4–5 brain slices, including those from the mPFC.
Incubate the slices in a reservoir chamber at 24°C–27°C for 30–60 min with ACSF.
Transfer one of the slices to the recording chamber on the stage of the DIC microscope.
Place a patch pipette towards a targeted pyramidal neuron under the DIC microscope.
Keep the temperature at 30°C–32°C during recording.
Choose relatively small and teardrop- or pyramidal-shaped neurons for clear identification of the soma.
Identify layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons morphologically or by fluorescence.
Approach the targeted neuron with positive pressure using the patch pipette.
Release the positive pressure to create a tight seal between the pipette and the neuron.
Change the holding potential from 0 mV to −70 mV gradually.
Generate a tight contact between the patch pipette and the membrane of the targeted neuron within several minutes, forming a giga-ohm seal.
Watch carefully how the cell responds to the change in holding potential.
Apply negative pressure by mouth or using a plastic syringe connected via tube to the glass pipette.
Connect the glass pipette to the targeted neuron.
Use small electrical stimulations called "Zap" if needed to establish connection between pipette and neuron.
Record the synaptic current after waiting about 5 minutes using stimulation protocols in the program with the amplifier.
Filter the recorded synaptic current at a range of 2.9 kHz.
Ensure the series resistance is below 20 MΩ, preferably 10 MΩ or less.
Control the series resistance throughout the experiment.
Record the synaptic currents from fluorescent-positive KD neurons or fluorescent-negative control neurons from the same electroporated mice.
Record spontaneous and/or miniature synaptic currents initially to check overall synaptic transmission in targeted neurons.
Record evoked synaptic responses by local electrical stimulation using a bipolar tungsten stimulating electrode if abnormalities in amplitude or frequency are found.
Place the bipolar tungsten stimulating electrode 50–100 μm away from recorded neurons to prevent direct stimulation of neurons.
Maintain consistent distances between the electrode and pairs of neurons with and without fluorescent proteins when analyzing the amplitude of evoked synaptic responses.
Record paired-pulse synaptic responses at several inter-stimulus intervals such as 20, 50, 100, and 500 msec.
Record paired-pulse responses at 20 ms inter-stimulus intervals.
Record paired-pulse responses at 50 ms inter-stimulus intervals.
Record paired-pulse responses at 100 ms inter-stimulus intervals.
Record paired-pulse responses at 500 ms inter-stimulus intervals.
Make slices from individual mice expressing Scr-miRNA or KD-miRNA plasmid co-expressed with Chronos-GFP under Cre-induced recombination.
Perform whole-cell patch clamp recording on the GFP-negative pyramidal neurons next to the opsin and GFP double-positive pyramidal neuron.
Apply paired-light-pulse stimuli at inter-flash intervals of 20, 50, 100, and 500 msec.
Compare PPR values between neurons showing Scr miRNA + opsin and KD miRNA + opsin.
Make slices where both pre- and postsynaptic neurons express KD miRNA and only presynaptic neurons express the opsin.
Locate pairs of mOrange-positive KD and negative control pyramidal neurons.
Perform whole-cell patch clamp recording on each pair of neurons sequentially.
Apply paired-light-pulse stimuli at inter-flash intervals of 20, 50, 100, and 500 msec.
Compare the amplitudes and PPR values between non-fluorescent control neurons and mOrange-positive KD neurons in the same slices.
Maintain blue LED light pulse strength at 4 mW/mm² and duration between 2−10 ms using an LED controller.
Set a bipolar tungsten stimulating electrode in layer 5/6 without any fluorescent signals in the electroporated mPFC.
Record paired-pulse-synaptic responses from appropriate pairs composed of GFP-positive and negative pyramidal neurons in layer 2/3 when stimulating layer 5/6 by the electrode.
Compare the amplitude and PPR values between GFP-positive KD and negative control neurons.
Perform immunohistostaining for GFP and mOrange in the slices to observe spine structures.
Stain the slices, including the GFP-positive Scr/KD neurons from independent Scr/KD mice, using anti-GFP and RFP antibodies.
Follow a general staining protocol.
Observe the spine structures using a confocal microscope.
Capture several images from each neuron (usually 5-6 images per neuron is optimal for quantification).
Count the number of spines present.
Measure the head-width of each individual spine using a program such as Neurolucida360.
Mix mOrange signal sparsely on GFP-positive pyramidal neurons for better visibility.
Alternatively, decrease the volume of injected miRNA-GFP vector to express GFP sparsely.
Use a 60× oil immersion objective with digital zoom 2.0 at 0.48 μm-z series (1024 × 1024 pixels resolution) for capturing confocal images.
Set outer range at 2.5 μm, minimum height at 0.3 μm, and detector sensitivity at 50% to detect spines.
Ensure detection requires a minimum of 10 voxels.
Classify spines based on head-to-neck ratio of 1.1 and length-to-head ratio of 2.5.
Define mushroom head size as 0.35 μm for spine classification.
Specify filopodium length at 3 μm for classification purposes.
Record evoked IPSC and evoked EPSC from the same pyramidal neuron to determine inhibition/excitation balance.
Record evoked EPSCs at the Cl− equilibrium potential initially (−40 mV).
Apply 50 μM D-AP5 to confirm suppression of evoked EPSCs.
Apply 10 μM NBQX to the bath solution to confirm suppression of evoked EPSCs.
Record evoked IPSC at 0 mV, the reversal potential of EPSC.
Apply 0.1 mM PTX to confirm suppression of evoked IPSC.
Correct for liquid junction potential calculated by composition of ACSF and each internal solution.
